approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would authorise spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the Parliamentary Departments.
It would provide funding equal to 7/12ths of the estimated 2020-21 annual appropriations for those departments.
The bill is one of three Supply Bills, each covering different types of government services as required by the Constitution.
Appropriates money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the Parliamentary Departments.
Sets the appropriation at 7/12ths of the estimated 2020-21 annual amount.
Separates the Parliamentary Departments' funding from ordinary annual services appropriations.
The Parliamentary Departments are affected by this bill.

The three supply bills—Supply Bill (No. 1) 2020‑2021 ($76.3 billion), Supply Bill (No. 2) 2020‑2021 ($6.7 billion), and Supply (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2020‑2021 ($150 million)—were moved to fund government operations for the first seven months of 2020‑21, with the federal budget rescheduled to 6 October 2020 due to coronavirus uncertainty. The bills include advance to the finance minister provisions of $16 billion and $24 billion for urgent expenditure, subject to additional transparency measures.

The speaker supported the supply bills, highlighting an unprecedented advance to the finance minister with new transparency measures requiring a press release for each use and opposition approval via Senator Gallagher for advances over $1 billion, and urged the government to release updated economic and budget forecasts to avoid a 10-month gap.

The speaker argued for the passage of three supply bills appropriating just under $83.2 billion for the first seven months of 2021, emphasising that the funding is interim and includes no new 2020-21 budget measures, only adjustments for COVID-19 and prior decisions.
